title: Allicin-loaded OSA-Pickering emulsion films: A novel edible coating for extending the shelf life of bananas
content:
by Yongjie Ma, Jiyu Bao, Yali Wang, Ye Chen, Hongliang Bao, Rongli Wang

In this study, an allicin-loaded Pickering emulsion edible film was prepared with octenyl succinic anhydride-modified starch (OSA-starch) as the particle emulsifier and applied to preserve postharvest bananas. Because emulsions containing 40–50% oil were stable but unsuitable for casting, a two-step dilution was used: a high-oil emulsion was first prepared and then diluted to an oil-to-water ratio of 1:9. Carboxymethyl cellulose (CMC) served as the film-forming matrix owing to its good dispersion and compatibility with the emulsion. FTIR spectra showed no new or vanished absorption bands, so allicin was retained physically in the matrix without covalent reactions; hydrogen bonding and hydrophobic forces are proposed as likely interactions, although FTIR alone cannot confirm them. The films blocked UV light almost completely between 200 and 350 nm yet stayed transparent to visible light, and 0.3% allicin gave the strongest shielding. On bananas stored for 15 days at 25 ± 1 °C and 70 ± 5% RH, the 0.3% coating (M-0.3) held weight loss to 8.0 ± 0.6% at day 12 against 18.6 ± 1.2% in the uncoated control (about 57% lower), kept pulp firmness at 21.0 ± 4.5 N at day 15, and stretched commercial acceptability from roughly 6 days to at least 15 days, outperforming all other formulations. The 0.3% level thus offered the best balance between preservation effect and allicin loading, and the coating provides a surfactant-free, food-grade option for active packaging of climacteric fruits.
